name: Vikas Varma Pokala
title: Full Stack Engineer
summary: Full-stack engineer with 2+ years of production experience building healthcare, telecom marketplace, and education-focused web systems. At a Toronto startup, owned backend development and shipped React UIs for two healthcare products—one deployed at the University of Toronto for pre-visit assessments and another used by 250+ doctors across Toronto clinics for clinical documentation. Also spent one year on contract at TELUS Marketplace, working across Java microservices and a Go + GraphQL middleware layer.

skills.Backend: Node.js, Express.js, Spring Boot, REST APIs, GraphQL, WebSockets, Kafka consumers, Microservices
skills.Cloud / DevOps: AWS (Transcribe, S3, KMS, CloudWatch), GCP, Firebase, Vercel, Docker
skills.Auth & Security: JWT, OAuth 2.0, Firebase Auth, encryption-at-rest, rate limiting
skills.AI Integrations: OpenAI, Gemini, Pinecone, RAG, Soniox, AWS Transcribe, Recall.ai

experience.title: Full Stack Developer – AI & Web Applications

project_blocks.project: Institution Digital Systems — Website, Email, and College Portal
bullets: Leading the redesign of the institution website and cleanup of its domain and official email setup, reorganizing public content and building reusable React components for academic, admissions, and institutional updates.

Architecting a role-based college portal with 1 shared sign-in and 3 tailored experiences for students, faculty, and administrators, using React with 2 backend service stacks: Node.js/Express.js with TypeScript and Java/Spring Boot.

Designing and building the attendance module around 5 core workflows—student and faculty mapping, daily attendance entry, record corrections, permission checks, and administrative review—with the data model prepared for future summaries and reporting.

Defining 4 additional academic workflows for phased delivery: results publishing, notes and resource sharing, announcements, and internal student–faculty communication, alongside the initial validation, testing, and deployment foundations.

project_blocks.project: CliniScripts — clinical documentation product for therapists, used by 250+ doctors
bullets: Joined as backend engineer when the product had ~100 active doctors; over six months, the platform scaled to 250+ doctors across Toronto clinics on the back of the work below.
Replaced AWS Transcribe with Soniox for live streaming, ran both providers in parallel for ~3 months, cut cost from ~$1.00/hr to ~$0.10/hr, and added support for 40+ languages.
Cut AI note-generation time from ~60s to ~20–30s by removing redundant backend steps and optimizing regex post-processing; added token streaming for live note rendering.

Led the security pass toward HIPAA-aligned workflows: added JWT-based service auth and OAuth 2.0 sign-in on top of password login, encrypted notes and audio at rest, and added per-endpoint rate limiting to stop subscription sharing across devices.

Integrated Recall.ai for virtual sessions on Google Meet, Zoom, Teams, and Webex: continuous transcript chunks coming in via webhook, handled with ordering and retry logic, then pushed to the frontend over WebSockets for live UI rendering.

Built an external integration product so partner companies could embed transcription and note generation under their own brand — separate API surface, dashboard for API-key issuance, usage tracked by hours and notes for billing, and developer documentation with sample code.
Alongside CliniScripts, shipped several short-cycle AI side projects for clinic and partner use cases — a few weeks each, backend owned start to finish.

project_blocks.project: TELUS Marketplace — IoT marketplace for enterprise customers
bullets: Owned the GraphQL signup endpoint, coordinating organization, customer, billing, password, terms, and email-confirmation flows across Java/Spring Boot microservices with cross-service error handling.
Built a reusable email-template API in a Java/Spring Boot Kafka consumer, added notification types, and fixed templating issues for multiple teams.

Wrote Go + GraphQL resolvers in the BFF middleware layer between the React frontend and Java microservices — aggregating across multiple backend endpoints and shaping responses to expose only the fields the frontend actually needed. First production Go work, code reviewed by senior TELUS engineers before every staging push.

project_blocks.project: CliniAssess — pre-visit questionnaire platform, used at the University of Toronto by 30+ doctors
bullets: Sole backend developer (no senior engineer above me) on a Node.js/MongoDB platform for pre-visit questionnaires — PHQ-9, GAD-7, OCD, substance-use, plus custom forms — sent to patients before their first appointment.
Designed a configurable form engine with multiple question types, answer-based branching, and scoring so administrators could manage forms without code changes.

Made the patient flow passwordless: unique per-assessment link in email, server-side state keyed to the link, so patients could pause mid-questionnaire and resume on another device without ever logging in.

Integrated OpenAI for end-of-assessment clinical summaries: JSON-schema structured output, per-form prompts, configurable summary length per doctor, plus failure handling for rate limits, malformed responses, and timeouts. Summaries stored with per-doctor retention policies (1 / 7 / 30 / 60 / 90 days).
Built the patient-facing React UI as a backend-configured form renderer, plus backend flows for doctor assignments, response review, summary editing, and University administration.
